subject: Archaeology
title: The Uluburun Shipwreck
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Uluburun Shipwreck usable.

hook.text: A sponge diver off Turkey found the richest ancient shipwreck ever — a 3,300-year-old floating department store.

buildup.text: The Uluburun wreck carried copper, tin, gold, ivory, amber, ebony, and glass from at least seven different cultures.

discovery.text: One ton of tin and ten tons of copper were on board — enough to make 300 bronze weapons.

twist.text: A golden scarab bearing Queen Nefertiti's name was among the cargo.

climax.text: The wreck proved that Bronze Age trade networks were far more connected and sophisticated than anyone had imagined.

punchline.text: One sunken ship rewrote the Bronze Age. The sea kept the evidence for 3,300 years.

quiz.question: What did the Uluburun shipwreck reveal about the Bronze Age?
options: Maritime trade did not exist before the Iron Age
Trade networks were far more connected and sophisticated than previously imagined
Only the Egyptians were capable of long-distance sea voyages
